mostWorthwhile.text: Adding hydrogen in two stages was most worthwhile: the hydroxyl intermediate made the formation of water on a grain understandable rather than a single unexplained leap.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial attempt to put oxygen directly on mixed dust was least clear: it instead automatically built the dusty cloud, so the need for shielding only became clear afterward.

surprise.text: I was struck that water ice can form on interstellar grains before planets exist, and that some of it may survive solar-system formation.

arbitrary.text: The initial dust-and-oxygen attempt felt somewhat arbitrary until the automatic result and subsequent cooling step explained why the grains needed a shielded environment first.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue to see how this pre-solar ice contributes to later worlds; the grain-surface chemistry gave that question a concrete starting point.
